newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - August 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - August 19.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Tuesday: IRISH INDEPENDENT - New court of appeal for exam students - Jinxed Mir station spins out of control in new chaos - Trade union opposes call for sell-off of Aer Lingus - Jobs safe at clothing giant Fruit of the Loom for one year, a SIPTU official said - Wilton & Horton half-year profits up 17 percent - Brewers face malt quality crux as grain prices slump - Ryanair ceases cargo operations next month - Stock markets hold their nerve but are braced for new falls - Pressure to revalue should be resisted, says economist IRISH TIMES - Minister wants 90 percent to sit Leaving Cert by the year 2,000 - German customs claim UK beef had Irish stamps - Strong rally in U.S. will boost European markets today - Profits up at Independent group paper - Private housing sector poised for record boom - Anxiety looms as Fruit of the Loom staff return from their holidays - Expansion brings DuPont funding in Derry to 478 million pounds - London Irish Rugby Club has had a good response in its funding operation
THE EXAMINER - Fake Irish certs used to beat UK beef ban - Ships on stand-by for end of cattle embargo - Anglers demand probe into handling of fish kill in County Limerick
